payload.name: Capture disclosed-recipient when announcing life events
payload.description: When a user message directly addresses a named person and announces a personal life event (e.g., marriage, job, move), also extract a memory that the event was told to that recipient, not just the event itself.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly addresses a named recipient (e.g., 'Hey [Name]!') and the speaker reports a personal life event, add a memory such as '[Speaker] told [Recipient] about [event]' using memory_kind 'relationship' or 'event', in addition to the event memory.
If later messages reveal more recipients of the same event, update or merge the disclosure memory rather than creating duplicates.

solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction recorded an announced life event but omitted the fact that the speaker disclosed it to the named addressee, so later questions like 'who was told' fail. The abstract mechanism is that a direct-address announcement (e.g., 'Hey [Name]! ... got married') implies a communication event distinct from the event itself. This rule applies whenever a session message explicitly greets or names a recipient and shares personal news; it does not apply to generic statements without a specific recipient.
